bugs.detail: On explicit cancel confirmation the bot returned the CUSTOMER_ID_REQUIRED message ('No pude verificar tu identidad', manage_appointments_tool.py:148) instead of cancelling. No tool_evidence captured across any of the 3 collector tiers (checkpoint/stream/db_turns) and no manage_appointments.idor_rejected warning was logged, indicating manage_appointments was never successfully invoked with a resolved customer_id (customer_id=None at tool entry). Customer exists in DB and AppointmentContextMiddleware injected 1 appointment for the customer, so the appointment lookup worked but the cancel-path identity resolution did not.

bugs.detail: Bot escalated to a human instead of self-service cancelling a >48h appointment. escalation_service fired (steps_completed=['db_record','admin_notification']; Chatwoot steps failed only because the sandbox conv_id is not a numeric Chatwoot ID — sandbox artifact). Root cause is upstream: the cancel path could not resolve customer_id, so the >48h policy-allowed self-service cancellation never executed and the bot fell back to escalation. Expected outcome 'cancelled' was not reached.

turns.milestone: Bot escalated to human; appointment remains CONFIRMED in DB.

bugs.detail: manage_appointments cancel path returned CUSTOMER_ID_REQUIRED ('No pude verificar tu identidad', manage_appointments_tool.py:148) on a >48h appointment owned by the resolved customer. No tool_evidence in any of the 3 collector tiers, no idor_rejected warning, and zero persisted conversation_turns.tool_calls — manage_appointments was never successfully invoked with a non-null customer_id. AppointmentContextMiddleware DID inject the appointment (lookup worked), so the failure is specific to customer_id resolution on the mutation/cancel path. Appointment stayed status='confirmed', cancelled_at=NULL.

After repeated identity-verification failures the bot escalated to a human (outcome=escalated) instead of cancelling. Expected outcome 'cancelled'. This is a DIFFERENT failure mode than V6 (V6 failed via R-37 chemical-safety escalation on the fever reason). N4 fix HELD — the fever/illness reason no longer triggers safety escalation — but a separate identity/customer_id resolution defect on the cancel path now blocks the cancellation.

notes: N4 fix held: fever/illness cancel reason did NOT trigger R-37 safety escalation (the V6 failure mode is GONE). However a SEPARATE critical defect surfaced: the manage_appointments cancel path could not resolve customer_id (returned CUSTOMER_ID_REQUIRED), so the >48h policy-allowed self-service cancellation never executed. The bot looped on identity-verification failures and ultimately escalated to a human. tool_calls_required ['manage_appointments'] NOT satisfied (no successful invocation captured). Appointment remains confirmed. Chatwoot 404s and Langfuse/OTLP 401s are sandbox/infra artifacts, not defects. NOT labeled sandbox_artifact because the cancel block is reproducible across 3 turns and is independent of the Chatwoot transport.
